subject: Penetration test scope clarification and interim evidence for FinWell
messages:
From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@finwell.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinWell Security <security@finwell.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: PT report, scope details and evidence of patching (SOC2 SIG follow-up)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the penetration test delivery last month. The FinWell security team is preparing our SIG and SOC 2 evidence pack and we need a few specific items to close out our attestation:

- The final PT report redacted for customer sharing (vendor name ok to show).
- A short (1 paragraph) description of the exact scope that was tested: public endpoints, internal admin console, and the k8s cluster ingress.
- Evidence of remediation for the 3 high findings called out in section 4 (screenshots / config snippets / Jira tickets).
- Any compensating controls you put in place while fixes were validated (WAF rules, RBAC changes, rate limiting).

We need these items by EOD PT on Monday (24 May) to keep our audit timeline. Can you confirm what we can share publicly vs. what must remain internal?

Thanks —
Elena
Elena Martin
Security Program Manager | FinWell Financial
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@finwell.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@thirdpartysec.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: PT report, scope details and evidence of patching (SOC2 SIG follow-up)

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick confirmation on scope and timeline: the test was executed by DeepGuard Labs (vendor visible in the redacted report) and covered the following attack surface we agreed to in scope:

- External public API endpoints (api.redwood.ai) including auth flows and token exchange.
- Customer-facing web console (console.redwood.ai) with standard admin workflows (login, role management).
- Kubernetes cluster control plane ingress and load balancer configuration for the us-west-2 production cluster (no access to customer data planes).

We can share a redacted PDF of the report suitable for customer-SOC/SIG attachments. We will NOT include DeepGuard internal notes or raw PoCs in the redacted copy — we can provide PoC detail under an NDA if FinWell's security team needs it for remediation validation.

On the remediation evidence: we have ticket records and screenshots for all three high findings. I'm attaching an interim evidence package (redacted report + tickets + portal screenshots) and a short compensating-controls summary describing the temporary WAF rules and rate-limits we enabled during remediation.

Note: one fix (ingress TLS cipher hardening) was applied and rolled out during the maintenance window on 2027-05-18; the k8s network policy change was implemented as a progressive rollout (canary -> full) with the Jira ticket linked below.

Deliverables attached: pt-summary-redacted.pdf, jira-6781-pt-fix-ticket.pdf, screenshot-portal-config-20270529.png, k8s-network-policy-snippet.txt

If you need additional artifacts (raw syslogs, full PoC steps), confirm the sharing NDA and we'll coordinate with DeepGuard.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@finwell.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinWell Security <security@finwell.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@thirdpartysec.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: PT report, scope details and evidence of patching (SOC2 SIG follow-up)

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick response. I reviewed the redacted report and the tickets. A couple of follow-ups before we mark the control as remediated in SIG: 

- For the k8s network policy change (Jira 6781) we need a short snippet showing the applied policy (namespace + ingress/egress rules) and a timestamped screenshot from the cluster console or kubectl output to prove rollout.
- For the WAF rules you mentioned, can you provide the rule IDs / deployment time and an example of the request block log for one of the exploit attempts? A redacted log is fine.
- The TLS cipher hardening fix: we need the ciphersuite list pre/post and the exact deployment time (UTC).

If you can get those three artifacts to us by EOD PT on Tuesday (25 May) we'll include them in our SIG evidence set.

Regards,
Elena
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@finwell.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: PT report, scope details and evidence of patching (SOC2 SIG follow-up)

Elena —

Attached are the three additional artifacts you requested: a small kubectl output (k8s-network-policy-snippet.txt) showing the namespace and ingress rules that were applied during the canary on 2027-05-17T22:10:30Z, a redacted WAF block log (included in jira-6781-pt-fix-ticket.pdf) with the rule IDs we deployed (WAF_RULE_2413, WAF_RULE_2414) and timestamps, and a TLS change summary in the redacted report that includes the pre/post ciphers list and the rollout time (2027-05-18T03:45:00Z UTC).

Quick notes:
- k8s change was a progressive rollout with 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 36 hours; the ticket contains the canary metrics and rollback window (no rollback required).
- WAF rules were temporary signatures added to the WAF-managed rule set; we've scheduled them for permanent rule tuning after the release cycle next quarter.
- If FinWell needs signed attestations from DeepGuard for remediation verification, they can request a separate validation engagement — we can facilitate.

Let me know if this completes your SIG bundle or if you need any additional signed artifacts.

Thanks —
Karthik

--
Attachments: pt-summary-redacted.pdf (redacted PT report, no PoCs), jira-6781-pt-fix-ticket.pdf (ticket + redacted logs), screenshot-portal-config-20270529.png (admin console showing role config change), k8s-network-policy-snippet.txt (kubectl output)
